newsitem.title: ISRAEL: High-tech toymaker tests Tel Aviv new issue market.
newsitem.headline: High-tech toymaker tests Tel Aviv new issue market.

text.p: Israeli toymaker Comfy Interactive Movies Ltd plans to raise between $25 million and $30 million in an initial public offering on the Tel Aviv market in May, Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull Securities Ltd said on Thursday.
The offering comes after a long dry period for the Israeli new-issues market and is a rare instance of a young, technology-oriented company opting to float domestically rather than in New York.
SocGen, one of three underwriters, has filed a draft prospectus with the Israeli Securities Authority.

David Cohen, of SocGen's corporate banking division, said Comfy's chief executive officer Itai Kohavi was attracted to the local and European marketplace rather than Nasdaq. "He feels the ratings on the Nasdaq are unsustainably high."

The company makes the Comfy Keyboard, a computer peripheral for children from one to three, and software for children up to age six. Comfy declined to comment on the offering, citing security regulations.
Kohavia said, "We will be the first start-up company to gain a domestic quote. The market is right and the timing is right."

The underwriters, who also include the Israeli brokerages IBI and Leader, hope to overcome the Tel Aviv market's weakness by selling up to half the offering to U.K. and European investors and by arranging a parallel quotation on London's SEAQ.

"With the (foreign) institutional interest already shown this will encourage the Israeli marketplace," said Cohen. "There should also be considerable (domestic) retail interest because it's a known product in Israel."
Cohen declined to say how much of the company would be floated or at what valuation. Three-year-old Comfy had sales of $3.8 million in calendar 1996 but declined to disclose profits.
SocGen said Comfy had 100,000 "installed units" and sells in 14 countries through distributors such as Tomy in Britain and France and the retail outlets Toys R Us and FAO Schwartz.

It also has alliances with MGM Interactive and recently signed an agreement to become the principal software supplier to Victor Co of Japan (JVC) for its new Family computer, which plugs into a television set.
The offering comes amid several planned big privatisations, which constitute about the only new issues in the Tel Aviv market.

The government is expected to go ahead with a secondary offering of about $165 million in Israel Discount Bank next month and Bank Leumi in May. The government is also weighing an offering for Bezeq Israel Telecom BEZEQ.TA that would be for about $450 million with a special tranche for foreign investors in July.
Israeli companies, most of them high tech, raised $629 million in initial public offerings in New York last year.
